Beam tracks image the He-3 target

run_145 · stat090_0000 · all four arms, A (det3) leading · nTOF partner 224670 · updated 2026-08-13 · PRELIMINARY

The waveform-first reconstruction, run on a fully nTOF-matched beam run, back-projects arm A's tracks to a compact source at the origin — the He-3 target is imaged. The reconstructed angle follows the point-source expectation tan θ = u / 235 mm across the plane, and the residual scale factor gives the first in-situ drift velocity at beam conditions: v ≈ 36.1 µm/ns, 15 % below the clean-gas Magboltz prior of 42.6. A second step — requiring an in-time hit in the SiPM wall segment the track points to and in the plastic bar behind it — confirms 3,761 tracks externally (51% of the predictable pool), with the extrapolated tracks landing in the correct 100 mm wall group and the segment ordering reproduced exactly. Everything on this page is on the full-coverage basis: the head-on band (|tan θ| < 0.08), which the hits-era slope_reliable gate used to discard, is measured natively by the forward fit and is the middle of the image.

What ran

run_145 (Aug 5, production statistics at the run_67 optimum: drift 700 V on all four chambers, resist A540/B540/C525/D520 V, Ar/iC4H10 90/10, 20 samples × 60 ns) is the only last-week run with full nTOF matching: the slim pipeline joins DREAM events to nTOF run 224670 on eventId at ~95 % efficiency, so every track knows which SiPM bars and plastics fired and when. The frozen (MPGD26-generation) wft/ forward-model reconstruction ran on the desktop over all four arms with bench-transferred calibration bundles (template + sharing kernel as hardware; v_drift seeded from Magboltz at 42.6 µm/ns), per-plane angle-mapping constants w0/kw applied, and the multi-track candidate sidecar on. Selection: both planes fit OK, |tan θ| < 1, and a same-arm in-time SiPM wall hit in the slim record. No slope gate — the June bench re-analysis measured the forward fit's head-on band unbiased (≤ 0.15°) at the same σ68 as the inclined bands, and at nTOF that band is the tracks that point straight at the target.

The image

The in-situ calibration

Positions never depend on v_drift; angles scale as 1/v. A ray from the origin crossing the strip plane at u must have tan θ = u/L exactly, so every inclined track measures the angle scale directly: ki = (ui/L)/tan θi. This is the one place the head-on band cannot contribute — k divides by tan — so the estimator keeps a |tan θ| > 0.1 floor.

quantityvaluecomment
v prior (Magboltz, clean 90/10, 233 V/cm)42.6 µm/nsbundle as seeded
v in-situ, imaging (arm A)36.1 µm/nsk = 1.18, |u| < 130 mm; coincident subset 1.24 → 34.4
bench wet-gas reference at this field23.3 µm/nsAr/iso 95/5 + H2O curve

36.1 sits between the clean-gas prediction and the wet bench curve — consistent with mildly wet gas after a month of flow, but deliberately quoted as an effective angle scale: the 20-sample readout window truncates the deepest columns and compresses large angles, and that compression is partially absorbed into k. For pointing and imaging purposes the effective scale is the right thing to use; separating true v from truncation needs the per-angle treatment.

What the head-on band adds

Dropping the slope gate is not a compromise — the newly admitted band images as sharply as the inclined tracks on every arm, at zero cost to any calibration number (it is k-invariant, which is precisely why it can never bias the scale):

Step 2 — the wall + plastic pointing coincidence

Every DREAM trigger is a same-arm SiPM-wall AND plastic coincidence, and the slim record says which wall segment (4 groups of 100 mm, 96 mm past the strips) and which plastic bar (two 200 mm bars, ~188 mm past the strips) fired. The second step extrapolates each track to both planes and requires an in-time hit (−100 < Δt < 60 ns) in the predicted segment and bar: 3,761 of 7,347 predictable arm-A tracks pass (51%). The head-on tracks take part — their prediction is position-dominated and needs no angle lever.

With and without the SiPM requirement

The same-arm wall-hit requirement is the baseline event selection above; these two comparisons show what it actually does. The DREAM trigger is an OR over arms, so a reconstructed track without a same-arm wall hit is usually a real track whose trigger came from elsewhere — the requirement removes about a fifth of tracks and mostly cleans edges.

The four fans — every arm, colored by its wall segment

The run_79 closing visual, remade on run_145 for all four arms at once: every wall-matched track, colored by the SiPM segment that triggered it, drawn through the 3D model. Two things should be visible per arm and both are, where the hardware allows: the four fans separate at the wall (that is the matcher + geometry) and sweep back through the He-3 capsule (that is the tracking). The number pair under each panel — the spread of the four bundle medians at the wall vs at the target plane — is the same statement measured; the shuffled-label null is the scale it has to beat.

D's high statistics (46k reconstructed events — twice the other arms) match its known occupancy. The v ordering A ≈ D > C is not yet a gas statement: C's number is bundle-limited and B's field is not nominal, so the clean gas-chain reading needs the C recalibration and the D anomaly closed first.

Sub-run 0001 — an independent hour, a new code generation

Sub-run 0001 was reconstructed with the post-restore wft (w0/kw applied inside the fit, angle_constants.applied stamped in the output metadata; the analysis detects the stamp and skips its post-hoc correction). Same chain, independent data, different code generation:

A1.24 (n=2,126)1.25 (n=2,417)3,761 / 4,153
D1.14 (n=154)1.65 (n=1,422)3,100 / 3,389
C1.49 (n=1,620)1.53 (n=1,909)3,410 / 3,907
B1.92 (n=394)1.23 (n=117)1,396 / 902

A and C reproduce to better than 3 %. D's single-number k moves — because D does not have a single angle scale. Splitting the per-track estimator by which side of the plane the track crossed:

armk (u>0 / u<0), sub-run 0000 k (u>0 / u<0), sub-run 0001
A1.09 / 1.271.09 / 1.29
D1.18 / 1.961.24 / 1.94

A's ~15 % side asymmetry is stable and is the expected signature of the un-surveyed in-plane offset u0 (it biases the two sides in opposite directions). D's ~60 % split is far too large for any offset and reproduces exactly across the two hours: its +u side agrees with the fleet (k ≈ 1.2) while its −u side wants k ≈ 1.9 — the same one-sided anomaly the wall crossings show, now measured as an angle scale. The apparent 0000→0001 shift in D's headline k was only the mixture weights moving with the coincident sample composition. B's k is unstable, as expected for an arm with no usable angle information.

What this does not show (yet)

  • The axial (Y) image is inconclusive. The y-plane pointing correlation is flat and the Y-profile of near-axis tracks (below) shows no clear capsule concentration — y-plane angle quality and the in-plane offsets need work before the second imaging coordinate is real.
  • In-plane offsets are un-surveyed. The strip-map zero per arm is provisional; the ~5 mm off-axis ridge in Fig 2 is its likely signature. A naive (u0, k) grid scan rails at its edge — the proper two-parameter likelihood fit is the open item.
  • Sub-run 0002 is not pulled yet. Sub-runs 0000 and 0001 are reconstructed and imaged (all four arms); the run's third hour is staged on EOS only.
  • Arm D's +u compression is unexplained. Reflection and map-mirroring are ruled out, the bench position scale is exact, and the wall instrumentation is healthy on that side — the remaining suspects are the beam-side geometry description of D's +u half or D's own reconstruction there. The per-side angle scale (previous section) is the same anomaly as a number: −u wants k ≈ 1.9 while +u agrees with the fleet. The multi-arm confirmed-track test is the queued instrument.
  • Single-k calibration. First-order only; the |u| > 130 compression is excluded, not corrected.
